newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks to sell same asset twice, report says.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks to sell same asset twice, report says.

text.p: President Clinton's aides have proposed to sell the same slice of the communications spectrum twice to fund proposed spending in the fiscal year that began last week, U.S. News and World Report said Saturday.

The White House initially planned to sell a part of the electromagnetic spectrum that carries radio, television and cellular signals to fund a proposed $1,500-a-year college tax credit, a centrepiece of Clinton's re-election effort.

But in recent negotiations with the Republican-led Congress over a request for $6.5 billion more in spending this year for education, the environment and technology, the White House tapped the same asset a second time for auctioning.

"After last week's shell-game spectrum sale, his college credit plan remains unfunded," the weekly newsmagazine said. The sale of the asset in question would raise $2.9 billion of the proposed $502 billion in discretionary spending for fiscal 1997, which began Sept. 30.
Asked to comment, the White House said it was actually Congress that had suggested using the very same piece of the spectrum as an offset to keep the budget on track to being balanced by 2002.

"Obviously, since we already proposed it (to finance the college scholarships) we supported the idea of selling that piece of the spectrum," said Lawrence Haas, a spokesman for the White House Office of Management and Budget.
He said that if Congress eventually enacted Clinton's request for so-called "Hope" scholarship funds, the administration would find a way to finance them "dime for dime."
